packageRules.description: A minor or patch update merges on green as a pull request into `ai/queue`, with no person in the loop; a major opens a pull request that waits for one. The rules below that hold, group or disable a package take it out of this default.

Nuxt 5 ships its fixes as nightly packages, so `nuxt` and the three `@nuxt/*` packages a module builds against are `npm:<name>-nightly@<tag>` aliases of a dist-tag: a lockfile refresh takes the newest nightly, and a nightly build is not a version Renovate can rank. Each name is matched beside its alias target. Replace the aliases with ranges and drop this rule once Nuxt 5 reaches `latest`.

`typescript` is aliased to `typescript-native-bridge` under `overrides:`, so a bump moves the bridge, the TypeScript behind it and `typescript-eslint` at once — a dedicated pass, never a routine update. A rule matches the resolved package name, so the alias target is named beside the alias.

`vue-tsc` 3.3.14 fixes the imported-ref `Property 'value' does not exist` of 3.3.12 (https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/issues/6237) and then reports the same TS2339 on an imported enum in a slot closure of a template holding a `//` in an attribute value, which `apps/web`'s `LinkMenuButton.vue` does (https://github.com/vuejs/language-tools/issues/6322), so it stays pinned exactly to 3.3.11, the last release that passes. Drop this rule and restore the catalog caret once a release fixes the issue.

`vize` 0.607.0 (#11043) stops treating an unresolved `useTemplateRef` as Vue's, so an auto-imported `useTemplateRef` (declared as `typeof import('vue').useTemplateRef` in each package's `auto-imports.d.ts`) types as `unknown`, and the template refs genshin-world and vue-phaserjs read fail typecheck (TS2339, TS2769, TS2322). 0.606.0 is green, and the same sources typecheck under vue-tsc. Drop this rule and restore the caret once ubugeeei-prod/vize#10980 is fixed and an auto-imported `useTemplateRef` types as Vue's again.

tsdown 0.23.3 moves its declaration plugin from 0.29.0-beta.2 to 0.28.8, and the size tests of genshin-interface, genshin-world and vue-phaserjs move with the declaration and bundle output, so the bump is a dedicated pass that reads that output before it lands. `@tsdown/css` pins its tsdown to the exact same version, so the two move together. Drop this rule and restore the carets once that output is checked.

The pair is pinned to one exact RC and moves as one, following the `rc` dist-tag: drizzle publishes a per-commit build (`1.0.0-rc.5-ab785fc`) under a tag per branch, and without the tag every one of those is a proposal. A release candidate can change what `db:gen` emits, so the grouped bump is read rather than merged on green. Drop `followTag` once 1.0.0 reaches `latest`.

`.node-version` is the one node pin, and `@types/node` follows its major with its own minors lagging node's, so the two move in one branch. The pin stays on its major until every environment that runs node can run the next one, and `references/node-major.md` is the checklist that says when. The change that moves the pin with `pnpm update:node <major>` raises this cap to the next major beside it.

A plugin's `engines.node` floor follows the pin, as `pnpm update:node` writes it. Renovate's default range strategy leaves a `>=` range the new version already satisfies, so the floor is bumped in the node branch beside `.node-version`.

pnpm ships its new workspace settings in minors (`autoDedupe` arrived in 12.6), and a setting this repo should turn on is visible only in the release notes, never in a green check. So the bot never merges a pnpm bump: each one is taken by the hand pass, which reads each release it crosses with `gh release view` and lands the settings worth taking in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` in the same commit, and the bot's PR for it is closed as superseded. `automerge: false` keeps that read-before-merge bump from merging unread.

A Docker digest moving under its tag is the publisher's routine rebuild — a patched base image republished under the same tag, versioned or not — so it lands on the same branch automerge the minor/patch rule above gives everything else. An action's digest is left out on purpose: an action ships a fix as a new tag, so a digest that moves under the same version is a re-pointed tag — the shape a SHA pin exists to catch — and it opens a PR for a person.
